text:
Sara (oncall): eu-west GPU pool is degraded ~60% capacity, autoscaler not reclaiming. Latency and 503s for a subset of customers. Suspect region-level networking flakiness. Initiating failover to us-east, need DNS plan.
Mike (netops): We have weighted A records in Route53. Current weight: eu-west 100, us-east 0. TTL is 300s on those records — recommend dropping TTL to 60 before changing weights.
Alicia (sre): Dropping TTL now. Updating Route53 record set via CLI.
Alicia (sre): ```json
{
  "Changes": [
    {"Action": "UPSERT", "ResourceRecordSet": {"Name": "inference.redwood.run.", "Type": "A", "TTL": 60, "SetIdentifier": "eu-west", "Weight": 100, "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "34.200.1.5"}]}}
  ]
}
```
deploy-bot: route53 change submitted: change ID /change/C123456789 (status: PENDING).
Sara (oncall): After TTL change we flipped weights to eu-west 0 / us-east 100. Still seeing ~25-30% traffic landing in eu-west.
Mike (netops): Expectation: resolver caches and some public DNS resolvers (Cloudflare/Google) may honor previous TTLs until expiry or due to EDNS caching. Also some ISP resolvers ignore our low TTLs; client-side caches exist.
Alicia (sre): Confirming via dig: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 inference.redwood.run A` returns eu-west IPs intermittently. Evidence of stale RRsets at resolver level.
dns-mon: Observed pattern: 8.8.8.8 and several European ISPs returning cached eu-west addresses. EDNS subnet shows per-edge caching. Sample: ";; ANSWER SECTION: inference.redwood.run.  300  IN A  34.200.1.5" even after change.
Mike (netops): Two mitigations: 1) force a separate health-failover via Route53 latency failover records (instant for our health checks) and 2) temporarily enable a short-lived HTTP redirect from eu-west edge to us-east ingress (if backend can accept). Redirect is invasive.
Alicia (sre): Started a health-based failover record set (route53 health checks) to mark eu-west unhealthy. That should make Route53 stop answering with eu-west IPs to resolvers that respect AWS health failover. Not instant for cached resolvers though.
Sara (oncall): We're also seeing customers with custom DNS (CNAMEs) still pointing at eu-west. Some corporate resolvers have very long cache retention. Triage: notify SRE/customer success to reach out to affected enterprise customers.
Mike (netops): Note for post-incident: set default TTL=60 for all failover/weight records, and add a pre-warm window where we flip small % of traffic before maintenance so caches propagate. Also document that CDN/edge caches can hold DNS-to-IP mappings and that invalidation isn't possible via DNS.
Alicia (sre): Filed runbook updates: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/dns-failover and added step to check resolver behavior with `dig +trace` and `dig @8.8.8.8 +short`. Example command we used: `dig +short @8.8.8.8 inference.redwood.run A; dig +short @1.1.1.1 inference.redwood.run A`.
Sara (oncall): We also temporarily increased capacity in us-east (burst pool) to absorb the extra load and raised preemptive autoscaler limits. Cost impact estimate ~+12% for the hour.
Alicia (sre): Monitoring shows tail traffic to eu-west declined to <5% after health failover and ~20 minutes of propagation. Full normalization ~40 minutes.
Mike (netops): Root cause note: regional network fabric intermittently dropped a subset of node egress, causing GPU autoscaler to misreport capacity. That triggered failover. Will include network vendor diagnostics.
Sara (oncall): Posting to status page and customer-notify channel. Creating postmortem and tagging this as DNS propagation/TTL issue + region failover.
Alicia (sre): Action items: update runbook TTLs, add pre-warm schedule, add explicit check for long-lived corporate resolvers, and test Route53 health-failover behavior during drills.
Sara (oncall): Thanks all. Filing postmortem: INC-1760001234. :white_check_mark:
